items.title: Communauté des Soufis : Message de remerciement à l’occasion du Maouloud 2026
items.description: Ceci est un message de remerciement de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis (C.I.S.) — Burkina Faso à l'occasion du Maouloud 2026 célébré sous le thème : « Cohésion sociale et tolérance religieuse ». Communauté Internationale des Soufis (C.I.S.) — Burkina Faso Au nom d'Allah, le Tout Miséricordieux, le Très Miséricordieux MESSAGE DE REMERCIEMENT À L'OCCASION DU MAOULID 2026 Thème : « Cohésion sociale et tolérance religieuse » Mes chers frères et sœurs, Au terme de la célébration du Maoulid 2026, placé sous le thème « Cohésion sociale et tolérance religieuse », je rends grâce à Allah qui nous a permis de commémorer ensemble, dans la paix et la ferveur, la naissance de notre bien-aimé Prophète Muhammad (paix et salut sur lui). Au nom de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis (C.I.S.) et en mon nom propre, j'adresse nos plus sincères remerciements à toutes celles et ceux dont la présence, la mobilisation, les prières et le soutien matériel, financier, moral ou spirituel ont donné à cette nuit bénie un éclat particulier. Nous exprimons toute notre gratitude à : Sa Majesté le Moogho NAABA BAONGO et aux chefs coutumiers ; El Hadj Saïd Kadré SAWADOGO, président de la Communauté Tidianite et patron de la cérémonie ; Au Grand Imam Boubacar YUGO, membre du présidium de la FAIB ; Aux autorités administratives et les forces de défense et de sécurité ; Nos frères chrétiens et les représentants des autres confessions religieuses ; Aux conférenciers, les partenaires, la presse et le comité d'organisation ; L'ensemble des disciples et fidèles venus de Ouagadougou, des provinces et de l'extérieur. Votre présence remarquable est la preuve vivante que le Burkina Faso peut demeurer uni et solidaire dans sa diversité. La foi au service de la fraternité La prière, le Saint Coran et la Bible sont des lumières qui guident nos pas. Mais ces lumières doivent transformer notre manière de vivre ensemble, dans la tolérance et l'acceptation de l'autre tel qu'il est. Celui qui prie sincèrement apprend à accueillir et à respecter son prochain : c'est là que la foi devient source de paix. Les Textes sacrés nous rappellent avec force cette exigence commune : Dans le Saint Coran : « Quiconque tue une personne sans que celle-ci ait commis un meurtre ou semé la corruption sur terre, c'est comme s'il avait tué toute l'humanité. Et quiconque lui sauve la vie, c'est comme s'il avait sauvé toute l'humanité. » (Sourate 5, verset 32). Allah appelle à la demeure de la paix et guide qui Il veut vers un chemin droit. » (Sourate Yûnus, 10:25) « Ô hommes ! Nous vous avons créés d'un mâle et d'une femelle, et Nous avons fait de vous des nations et des tribus pour que vous vous entre-connaissiez. Le plus noble d'entre vous auprès d'Allah est le plus pieux. » (Sourate 49, verset 13) « Les croyants ne sont que des frères. Établissez donc la réconciliation entre vos frères et craignez Allah afin qu'il vous soit fait miséricorde. » (Sourate 49, verset 10) « Ô vous qui avez cru ! Entrez pleinement dans la paix et ne suivez point les pas du diable, car il est pour vous un ennemi déclaré. » (Sourate 2, verset 208) Dans la tradition prophétique (Hadith) : D'après Abou Hourayra (qu'Allah soit satisfait de lui), le Messager d'Allah (paix et salut sur lui) fut interrogé sur ce qui fait entrer le plus de gens au Paradis. Il répondit : « La crainte révérencielle d'Allah (la piété) et le bon comportement. » Dans la Bible : « S'il est possible, autant que cela dépend de vous, soyez en paix avec tous les hommes. » (Romains 12:18 — un appel universel adressé à toute l'humanité) « Heureux ceux qui procurent la paix… » (Matthieu 5:9) « Ce que vous voulez que les hommes fassent pour vous, faites-le de même pour eux. » (Luc 6:31) « Mais moi, je vous dis : Aimez vos ennemis, bénissez ceux qui vous maudissent, faites du bien à ceux qui vous haïssent. » (Matthieu 5:44) « Ainsi donc, recherchons ce qui contribue à la paix et à l'édification mutuelle. » (Romains 14:19) Un engagement renouvelé pour le Burkina Faso. Si le Coran nous exhorte à nous connaître malgré nos différences, à être justes envers tous et à entrer pleinement dans la paix, et si le Prophète (paix et salut sur lui) place le bon comportement au sommet des vertus, comment pourrions-nous prétendre bâtir la paix en nous contentant de prier et de lire les Livres saints tout en cultivant la division ou la haine ? La prière véritable exige le respect et l'acceptation de l'autre. Le véritable croyant ne construit pas sa grandeur en humiliant celui qui croit autrement ; il démontre sa foi par sa capacité à aimer, à pardonner et à vivre en paix. La religion doit être un pont entre les hommes, jamais un mur qui les sépare. Si nous prions le même Dieu, Créateur de l'humanité, nos lieux de culte doivent être des écoles de paix, nos prières des sources de fraternité et nos religions des chemins de dignité humaine. Telle est la devise du Maoulid et de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis (C.I.S.) : « Plusieurs religions, différentes croyances, mais une seule humanité : apprenons à vivre ensemble dans la paix, le respect et l'amour. » Continuons donc à méditer les Écritures et à traduire leurs enseignements en actes concrets de tolérance, de pardon et de solidarité. Nous formulons le vœu que ce Maoulid ne soit pas seulement une célébration ponctuelle, mais le point de départ d'un engagement durable en faveur de la cohésion sociale. Qu'Allah accepte nos prières, récompense chacun de vous, bénisse vos familles et fasse régner durablement la paix dans notre cher Burkina Faso. Vivre la paix partout et pour tous. Un prochain n'est pas un ennemi. Encore merci à toutes et à tous pour votre confiance et votre accompagnement. Le Guide spirituel Cheikh Soufi Moaze OUEDRAOGO Président fondateur de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis (C.I.S.) Lire aussi : Burkina : La communauté des soufis commémore le Maouloud sous le signe de la cohésion sociale et de la tolérance religieuse

items.title: Tunisie | Debbache appelle à réduire les droits de douane des composants automobiles importés
items.description: La Chambre nationale des concessionnaires et des constructeurs automobiles (CNCCA) propose une réduction des droits de douane appliqués aux composants automobiles importés, destinés à la fabrication et à l’assemblage en Tunisie. Cette initiative vise à encourager l’investissement local, à proposer des véhicules neufs à des prix adaptés au pouvoir d’achat des citoyens, et à limiter l’expansion du marché parallèle. Ibrahim Debache, président de la Chambre, a déclaré vendredi 13 novembre 2026, à Mosaïque FM , que cette proposition avait été soumise à la Commission des finances du Parlement — dans le cadre des auditions relatives au projet de loi de finances pour 2027 — afin de trouver des solutions pour dynamiser le secteur de la construction et de la distribution automobile. La baisse du quota annuel de véhicules alloué aux concessionnaires agréés, conjuguée à la hausse des prix des voitures neuves — désormais inadaptés au pouvoir d’achat des citoyens —, constitue l’un des principaux facteurs poussant les consommateurs à se tourner vers le marché parallèle pour acquérir des véhicules d’occasion, a indiqué M. Debbache, en ajoutant que ces véhicules ne sont pas nécessairement adaptés aux spécificités du marché tunisien, qu’il s’agisse de l’état des infrastructures routières, de la qualité du carburant ou des conditions climatiques. Dans ce contexte, M. Debbache a insisté sur la nécessité de favoriser la production locale, une solution susceptible de répondre à une partie de la demande intérieure et de proposer des véhicules neufs à des prix compétitifs. Il a fait remarquer, à ce propos, que la construction automobile en Tunisie est confrontée à plusieurs difficultés, notamment l’application de droits de douane sur les composants importés, suivie de l’imposition de taxes à la consommation lors de la commercialisation du véhicule après sa fabrication et son assemblage, déplorant ce qu’il a qualifié de «situation de double imposition, qui entrave la compétitivité des véhicules fabriqués localement» . Les huit usines actuellement actives dans ce secteur rencontrent des difficultés, a indiqué M. Debbache, en préconisant, a minima, la suppression des droits de douane sur les composants automobiles importés destinés à la production locale ; une mesure qui permettrait de réduire les coûts de production et de renforcer la compétitivité du produit tunisien. Le responsable syndical a par ailleurs noté qu’une telle décision aiderait à satisfaire les besoins du marché intérieur, mais pas seulement, car elle pourrait aussi, à terme, ouvrir des perspectives pour l’exportation des véhicules fabriqués en Tunisie. Le président de la Chambre nationale des concessionnaires et des constructeurs automobiles a également préconisé l’intégration de cette proposition au projet «Une voiture pour chaque famille» — initialement prévu dans la loi de finances 2026 mais resté lettre morte, en soulignant que la production locale pourrait constituer un levier concret pour concrétiser cette initiative, en permettant aux familles d’acquérir des véhicules neufs à des prix adaptés à leurs capacités financières. Tout en s’interrogeant sur les raisons pour lesquelles les citoyens ne se voient pas offrir la possibilité d’acquérir un véhicule neuf à un prix abordable — à l’instar du dispositif des «voitures populaires» , dont le quota annuel est d’environ 10 000 unités, M. Debbache a fait valoir que l’encouragement de la production locale contribuerait à élargir l’offre, à proposer de nouvelles alternatives aux consommateurs et à limiter le recours au marché parallèle. items.title: Police foil attack on checkpost in KP's Bannu, eliminate four terrorists
items.description: BANNU: Police foiled a terrorist attack on Kingar Pul Police Checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu district on Friday night, eliminating four terrorists in retaliation, a police spokesperson said. According to the police spokesperson, heavily armed terrorists launched a sudden attack on the checkpost last night. “However, police personnel deployed at the checkpost responded promptly and successfully repelled the assault,” he stated. Following the incident, the Rapid Response Force (RRF) and additional police personnel were rushed from Police Lines to the scene. They cordoned off the area and launched a clearance and search operation, the spokesperson added. “During the operation, the bodies of four terrorists were recovered,” he added. The spokesperson said that police also seized four Kalashnikov rifles, several magazines, a substantial quantity of ammunition, hand grenades and bandoliers, adding that the identification of the slain terrorists was underway. Meanwhile, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed commended Bannu Police for foiling the attack. He said successfully repelling the assault under the cover of darkness reflected the high level of training, vigilance and bravery of police personnel. The IG added that effective operations were underway under a comprehensive strategy to eliminate terrorism and rid the province of the menace. “Protecting the lives and property of the public remains the top priority of the police,” IG Hameed said. Yesterday, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the security forces had killed 74 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in KP and Balochistan. Two days ago, terrorists also attacked Bandkorai Police Station in Dera Ismail Khan by ramming an explosives-laden pickup into its main gate, triggering a powerful blast followed by intense gunfire. However, prompt retaliatory fire by police personnel prevented the attackers from entering the police station, forcing them to flee. On the same day, however, two policemen, including an assistant sub-inspector (ASI), were martyred in Swabi when three suspects opened fire on a patrolling party.

items.title: 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’
items.description: Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time. The nationwide stop on Friday sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks. The ground stop lasted around four hours and was lifted at 8:15 pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday). Federal Aviation Administration officials reopened the airspace on Friday night “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations… Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” Duffy said. Administration officials blamed the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment, adding there was no evidence of foul play. “This is a legacy system problem,” Duffy said. “We have old, old switches, old routers. “We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.” Duffy had formally asked Congress on Thursday for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control System. As the ground stop was lifted, he repeated his plea. “I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said. 6,000 flights canceled There were almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes, according to FlightAware, a tracking platform. Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways. Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their plans into chaos. “We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California. A nationwide ground stop is highly unusual. There was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks in September 2001, when no aircraft took to the skies for days. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stressed there was no evidence of any hostile action on Friday. “We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or (AI) attack,” he told a news conference. He also ruled out any connection with the outage that affected Microsoft this week, knocking email systems offline for millions of users, public services and businesses worldwide. Confusion and delays The stop caused misery at airports around the country. At New York’s LaGuardia Airport, Tiara Johnson said she had been trying to get to Orlando for a concert with a friend. “They just keep delaying it… So it started out at 7:55. Then it went to 8:30, 9:30. Now it’s at 10:30. So we don’t know when it’s gonna leave,” she told AFP. “I feel very frustrated because you know, you come to the airport and then all of a sudden your whole plans have changed and you don’t know when you’re leaving. We’re kind of stuck.” Some travelers said they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could. Boards at the airport continued to show departures leaving as normal, while mobile boarding passes held by those stuck on the ground appeared to show their flight was underway. Stranded passengers were scrambling to find alternatives, with long lines forming at rental car counters at the airport in Las Vegas. Susan Sardina said she had boarded her flight back to Orange County, California when staff told passengers there was a problem. “We were already on our flight to leave and we were told to get off,” she told AFP as she stood in a lengthy queue for a rental car. For those looking on the bright side, the delay was a chance to extend a break. Kathy Sommers was on her way home from visiting friends in Las Vegas when her flight got canceled. “We’re blessed that our friends are coming back to pick us up,” she said. “So one more night to play cards.” Vanguard News The post 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Delta 2027: Omo-Agege challenging political establishment he helped to build
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi For a politician who once occupied the number three position in Nigeria’s constitutional order, served two terms in the Senate and declared that he had completed his legislative assignment, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege’s decision to seek a return to the Red Chamber presents an intriguing twist in Delta State’s changing political history. More intriguing is his choice of Delta Central, the district he represented for eight years. He is now facing Senator Ede Dafinone, the incumbent he helped bring into the Senate in 2023, but who now belongs to the political establishment that has taken over the party Omo-Agege once controlled in Delta. It is a contest laden with political irony, bruised relationships and competing ambitions, raising questions about whether personal political capital can survive the collapse of an established political structure. Today, Omo-Agege is seeking a Senate return on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), while Dafinone remains the APC incumbent, backed by a party now accommodating much of Delta’s former PDP political establishment. From Ibori’s government to the Senate Omo-Agege’s political journey has taken him through government, opposition politics and national legislative influence. A lawyer, he began his major political career under former Governor James Ibori, serving as Executive Assistant, Commissioner for Special Duties and later Secretary to the Delta State Government between 2003 and 2007. After leaving government, he returned to private business and political mobilisation, eventually emerging as senator representing Delta Central in 2015. His re-election in 2019 elevated his stature further. He became Deputy President of the Ninth Senate, placing him among the most influential political officeholders from the Niger Delta. But in 2023, he abandoned the familiar senatorial contest to challenge for the governorship under the APC against Sheriff Oborevwori, the PDP candidate and successor to former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa. It was a bruising contest that divided political loyalties across Delta. Oborevwori eventually polled 360,234 votes against Omo-Agege’s 240,229, ending his immediate governorship ambition but not his political relevance. The Political Tsunami And The Lost Territory The defining rupture came in 2025. Before Oborevwori and Okowa moved into the APC, Omo-Agege openly challenged their proposed entry. At an APC stakeholders’ engagement in February, he declared that the two leaders had no moral ground to abandon the PDP, a party they had repeatedly described as insurmountable in Delta. He insisted they should remain in the PDP and rebuild the structure they had once celebrated. He argued that the APC had already established itself in Delta, winning two senatorial seats and other legislative positions in 2023, and did not need the wholesale arrival of politicians who had spent years presenting the PDP as unbeatable. But on April 23, 2025, Oborevwori, Okowa and a formidable assembly of former PDP political officeholders defected to the APC. The development fundamentally altered the balance of power. Interestingly, after the defection became reality, Omo-Agege issued a statement welcoming the governor and other defectors, describing their entry as a significant milestone for the APC and urging existing members to embrace them. That public welcome, however, did not settle the question of who would control the party’s political machinery. The former PDP establishment arrived with the governor, former governor, lawmakers, local government structures and a substantial political network. For Omo-Agege, the challenge became how to retain influence within an APC whose internal balance had changed dramatically. Dafinone: From political successor to rival The relationship with Dafinone gives the 2027 contest another dimension. In 2023, Omo-Agege vacated the Senate seat to pursue the governorship, with Dafinone emerging as the APC candidate for Delta Central. Dafinone won and became his successor. Three years later, the succession arrangement has become a contest for the same seat. At the APC senatorial primary in May 2026, the party’s committee declared Dafinone winner with 116,252 votes against Omo-Agege’s 3,643. Omo-Agege disputed the outcome, claiming results collated from the district’s 85 wards showed he had won. He subsequently resigned from the APC, joined the NDC and declared his intention to contest Delta Central again. What might have been an internal party contest has consequently become a direct political confrontation across party lines. For Dafinone, it is an opportunity to defend his mandate. For Omo-Agege, it is a bid to reclaim the seat he relinquished for a governorship ambition. The strength of political fighter Omo-Agege’s political appeal rests on his combative disposition, national connections and ability to remain politically visible outside government. His supporters see a politician who does not easily surrender political ground. His journey from the Ibori administration to the Senate, re-election in 2019 and emergence as Deputy Senate President demonstrate a career built through successive political contests. His 2023 governorship campaign also established him as a major challenger to the PDP’s dominance, despite his defeat. Now, as the NDC’s most recognisable political figure in Delta, he hopes to translate that personal profile into a broader opposition identity. His confidence is reflected in his declaration: “We are contesting the 2027 general elections on the platform of the NDC and we are going to win. “We will win because people power will ultimately defeat godfather power and empty boast in the general election. “We know they will try to manipulate or rig as they always do because that is the only way they can win but we will stop them.” He invoked former US President Abraham Lincoln’s description of democracy as government of the people, by the people and for the people, declaring that a new Nigeria was possible. It’s important to note that personal political following is not the same as an organised electoral structure. Omo-Agege must demonstrate that his network can operate outside the APC, particularly in a state where influential politicians, elected officials and established political structures have converged under the ruling party. The NDC must build ward-level organisation, attract alliances, secure agents and demonstrate the funding and mobilisation capacity required for a serious electoral contest. There is also the question of public perception. Among some political observers, criticism of Omo-Agege centres on allegations that political benefits and opportunities have not been sufficiently distributed beyond his immediate political circle and community. Such perceptions, whether justified or not, could become an issue in a contest requiring support across Delta Central’s eight local government areas. His combative political language is another double-edged issue. At a campaign gathering in Uvwie on October 23, he introduced the expression, “Rig and die”, warning against electoral manipulation and threatening those involved in rigging. His media aide subsequently explained that the warning was directed at electoral manipulators and ballot snatchers, not ordinary voters. Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo also entered the debate, questioning the issues surrounding the expression. For Omo-Agege, the challenge is to defend electoral integrity without allowing threatening language to overshadow his political message. Senate Return: An unfinished assignment? There is an undeniable irony in Omo-Agege’s return ambition. Having once occupied the Senate’s leadership hierarchy, he is seeking another mandate from the same constituency after opting out of the seat to pursue the governorship. His earlier suggestion that he had completed his legislative assignment makes the comeback particularly interesting. Is the return driven by an unfinished political project, a desire to recover lost influence or a conviction that Delta Central requires his experience in the Senate? His ambition is also tied to the wider NDC project. With governorship candidate Chris Iyovwaye yet to command the same public recognition as Omo-Agege, the former Deputy Senate President has become the party’s central political face in Delta. Whether that personal prominence can translate into a functioning opposition organisation remains another test. Meanwhile, Dafinone has the advantage of incumbency and the political resources available to a senator seeking re-election under the governing party. In 2023, Omo-Agege challenged Oborevwori from the commanding position of Deputy Senate President and APC governorship candidate. In 2027, he approaches another contest from outside the party he once led in Delta. The former Senate leader is back, seeking to reclaim the seat he left behind. This time, the battle is not simply against Dafinone. It is against a transformed political establishment, a changed party landscape and the weight of expectations surrounding his own political record. For Omo-Agege, the 2027 Senate ambition is more than a return to the Red Chamber. It is a test of how much political capital remains when the structure that once carried it has moved elsewhere. items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : La facture électronique certifiée au cœur de la 2e session ordinaire de la CNLF
items.description: La Commission nationale de lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) a tenu, le 12 novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, sa deuxième session ordinaire de l’année, consacrée à la Facture électronique certifiée (FEC). Cette rencontre a permis de sensibiliser les acteurs économiques sur les enjeux et les avantages de cette réforme fiscale. Introduite dans le Code général des impôts par la loi de finances 2025, la FEC vise à renforcer la transparence et la traçabilité des transactions commerciales. À travers deux communications animées par des experts de la Direction générale des impôts (DGI), les participants ont été informés sur le cadre juridique, le fonctionnement et les conditions d’adhésion au dispositif. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur les avantages de la facturation électronique pour les entreprises et l’État. Elle permet aux entreprises d’améliorer leur gestion comptable et de faciliter leurs obligations fiscales. Pour l’administration fiscale, elle constitue un moyen de renforcer le contrôle des transactions et d’améliorer la mobilisation des recettes publiques. Pour le coordonnateur de la CNLF, le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, ce système ‹‹ est un outil de traçabilité pour la bonne gestion. Sous le leadership du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, nous avons choisi une démarche de souveraineté économique. Cette souveraineté économique nécessite l’accompagnement des entreprises; d’où ce thème qui interpelle les opérateurs économiques à une adhésion massive ››, a-t-il expliqué. Cette deuxième session a été placée sous la présidence de la gouverneure du Guiriko, représentée par son secrétaire général Souleymane Nakanabo. Il a salué la tenue de cette session et invité les participants à des échanges francs pour qu’à la sortie de cette rencontre la Facture électronique certifiée n’ait plus un secret pour eux. Les discussions ont également permis aux participants d’obtenir des éclaircissements sur les modalités pratiques de mise en œuvre de cette réforme et la nécessité d’accompagner les entreprises dans leur transition numérique. À travers cette session, la CNLF entend contribuer à l’assainissement de l’environnement économique, à la bonne gouvernance des entreprises et au renforcement de la mobilisation des ressources publiques au Burkina Faso. L’article Bobo-Dioulasso : La facture électronique certifiée au cœur de la 2e session ordinaire de la CNLF est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: 2027: Presidential choice exposes widening elite-grassroots divide in South-East
items.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South East The scene at the School of Health Aba, the commercial capital of Abia State last weekend offered a fascinating glimpse into what could become one of the defining political contradictions of the 2027 presidential election. It showed the widening gulf between the political calculations of South East power brokers and the apparent preferences of the ordinary people. It was a moment when political establishment encountered popular sentiment, and the response from the crowd was anything but pretence. The masses, in unmistakable terms, passed a strong message: they are not in for jokes! They know what is good for them. While a significant section of the South East political establishment, including governors, National Assembly members and other influential politicians, has either openly or tacitly aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election ambition, the grassroots appear to be gravitating in a different direction, with the former Anambra State governor, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, flag bearer, Mr Peter Obi, retaining a formidable following across the region. The drama unfolded when Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, attended the 2026 Item Day organised by the Item people in Aba. Kalu hails from Bende town, a neighbouring community with Item. As a prominent supporter of President Tinubu, Kalu apparently saw the gathering as an opportunity to canvass support for the President ahead of 2027. He never wanted to miss the opportunity, and rightly so. But what followed was a political moment he might not have anticipated. He never dreamed of the dramatic turn of events as he grabbed the microphone to market Tinubu’s candidacy. Dressed in the traditional Igbo (isiagu) attire, with a red cap to match, Kalu who prides himself as ‘the number six’ man in the country, mounted the stage and urged the people to support Tinubu’s re-election, assuring them that the President would do more for Abia if given another mandate. ‘Tinubu’ to ‘Obi kererenke’ “Tinubu will do more for Abia. Vote for Tinubu in 2027. He is the best for Nigeria,” he told the gathering. But as the Deputy Speaker shouted “Tinubu”, apparently expecting an enthusiastic response from the crowd, what came back was a thunderous rendition of “Obi kererenke”, the popular solidarity chant associated with Peter Obi. The response was spontaneous, collective and blunt! Even with a microphone, Kalu’s voice appeared drowned by the surging chants of the crowd. Attempts to calm the gathering did little to change the mood. Neither his assurance of a proposed federal university for Item nor the intervention of a performing artiste, who quickly introduced another Tinubu campaign song, “On Your Mandate We Shall Stand”, could dislodge the crowd’s enthusiasm for Obi. The Obi chants persisted, leaving the Deputy Speaker visibly taken aback. At a point, he wondered whether the people before him were genuinely Item indigenes. But his question over the true identity of the crowd, perhaps, was more rhetorical than practical. It was a community thing and there was no mixed audience as the people could easily identify themselves. There was little reason to suggest any infiltration or invasion by outsiders. Apparently sensing the mood, Kalu eventually abandoned the political solicitation, bringing an unexpected end to what was meant to be a campaign opportunity. A video of the incident has since circulated widely on social media, generating conversations about the actual reach of the South-East political establishment among its constituents. Beyond the embarrassment or amusement the episode may have generated, it raises a more consequential question: Can the political elite deliver the South East electorate to a presidential candidate whose popularity among ordinary voters appears considerably weaker than the influence of those championing his cause? The South East presents an interesting political paradox. With the recent defection of Gov. Peter Mbah of Enugu State to the APC, the APC now controls three out of five states in the zone – Imo, Enugu and Ebonyi states, while Anambra is governed by the APGA which has formally endorsed Tinubu. The governors of these states have various degrees of political alignment with the Tinubu administration, with several influential politicians from the region also playing prominent roles in the President’s political calculations. Even Abia Governor, Dr Alex Otti, who shared a political platform with Obi in 2023, has, on several occasions, avoided positioning himself as an opponent of Tinubu’s re-election bid. Otti has also not openly canvassed support for Obi. Yet, the apparent enthusiasm for Obi among sections of the grassroots suggests that political alignment at the top may not necessarily translate into electoral compliance at the bottom. There are several reasons this disconnect may persist. And dismissing these underlying factors with a wave of the hand is politically suicidal. Obi’s appeal First is Obi’s enduring appeal, built around his reputation for prudence in public finance, perceived administrative discipline, personal integrity and the promise of a different approach to governance. Whether his supporters’ expectations can be translated into electoral victory is another matter, but his emotional connection with a significant section of the South East electorate remains a political factor that cannot be wished away. There is also the unresolved Nnamdi Kanu question.The continued detention of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPoB) leader remains a sensitive issue in the region. Many residents view his incarceration as unjustified and have continued to appeal for his release. For such people, the Federal Government’s handling of the matter has become an important measure of its disposition towards the South East. Many are still struggling to understand the justification behind Kanu’s continued incarceration at a time bandits and mass muderers are enjoying state pardon under the guise of repentance. Yes, Kanu was not arrested and renditioned under Tinubu but he was sentenced to life imprisonment under him. And for one year his efforts to appeal his conviction have continued to suffer inexplicable setbacks. Consequently, assurances by political office holders from the region that the APC government has the South East at heart may not be enough to erase the reservations of voters who believe that more decisive action should have been taken on Kanu’s case. Infrastructure and economic inclusion are other issues shaping public perception.The prolonged neglect of the Eastern railway corridor, particularly the failure to restore regular train services along the route since 2015, remains a source of concern. This is especially so against the backdrop of federal investments in railway infrastructure in other zones oy the country. The removal of sections of the old railway tracks in the region in anticipation of rehabilitation and replacement, has further heightened concerns among residents who are yet to see the promised transformation. There is also the broader question of equity in the distribution of political power and national opportunities. Nearly six decades after the Nigerian Civil War, the South East is yet to produce a democratically elected president. For many in the region, this remains an uncomfortable symbol of their perceived exclusion from the highest level of national political leadership. While political office holders may consider strategic alignment with the centre even at the expense of their people a practical route to securing federal attention and influence, ordinary voters may see the matter differently. Their expectations are not necessarily limited to access to the corridors of power; they also include fairness, recognition, infrastructure and a sense of belonging. Precedents in South-East To be fair, the South East’s experience under successive administrations cannot be reduced to the policies of one political party. Nor can every development challenge in the region be blamed exclusively on the current Federal Government. However, perceptions, whether entirely justified or otherwise, often carry considerable weight in electoral politics. The Item Day incident may not necessarily represent the opinion of every South East voter, and a spontaneous crowd reaction at a cultural festival cannot substitute for the verdict of the ballot box. But it offers a revealing indication that the political preferences of the grassroots should not be taken for granted. The 2027 election may therefore test not just the strength of the APC’s political structure in the South East but also the ability of its influential political figures to persuade their constituents to embrace a presidential project they appear less enthusiastic about. The political elite are entitled to their choices, just as the masses are entitled to theirs. Neither political office nor proximity to power confers ownership of the electorate’s conscience. Ultimately, the 2027 presidential election will not be decided by endorsements, political calculations, campaign songs or the number of influential personalities standing behind a candidate. It will be decided by voters, one ballot at a time. The South East political establishment may have its preferred presidential destination, but the grassroots appear determined to have a say in choosing their own route. The masses are beginning to prove that they, not the elite, are ‘the lion of the South East’. Whether that mood will survive the pressures, negotiations and realignments of the campaign season remains to be seen. One thing, however, is increasingly clear: no political party should mistake the support of the elite for an automatic endorsement by the people! items.title: Wasim Akram questions Cummins’ Sandpapergate denial, says bowlers would spot tampering
items.description: Pakistan pace legend Wasim Akram has questioned Australia captain Pat Cummins’ claim that he was unaware of the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, arguing that any experienced bowler would immediately recognise the difference between natural wear and deliberate damage to the ball. Speaking in a video posted on social media on Saturday from Melbourne, Wasim said the marks left by sandpaper were distinctly different from those caused by normal contact with the ground. “As a bowler, I’ll have a look at the ball and know straight away something is not right,” Wasim said. “He said he didn’t know (about the use of sandpaper). As a bowler, when the cricket ball comes into my hand, whether it’s the fifth over, the tenth over or the fiftieth over, you look after the ball, you shine one side of the ball. But the sandpaper scratch is totally different than the one-bounce scratch.” Wasim suggested that the difference could easily be identified through a simple comparison, saying anyone could take a semi-new ball, rub sandpaper against it and observe the resulting marks. The former Pakistan captain, widely regarded as one of the finest exponents of reverse swing, described Cummins as “a very close friend” and insisted he was not taking sides in the controversy, which has resurfaced following revelations by former Australia opener Usman Khawaja in his autobiography Sabr. Khawaja alleged that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was widespread within the Australian dressing room, including among the bowling group, during the 2018 tour of South Africa. At the time, Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town. Then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Bancroft subsequently received suspensions, while Cricket Australia undertook a wider cultural review. Cummins, however, rejected Khawaja’s allegations during a lengthy press conference in Sydney on Friday, describing them as “100 per cent wrong” and “complete and utter nonsense”. The Australia captain maintained that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field and denied being an architect of the ball-tampering scheme. He also said he was genuinely shocked to learn that Khawaja had warned Bancroft to be careful while using the sandpaper. Wasim said the controversy had also raised wider questions about Australia’s reputation for honesty and sportsmanship. “Australians are famous for their straightforwardness, their hardness on the field and off the field, and most importantly honesty. I think that’s why the whole nation has been under stress a bit,” he said. “I hope things get sorted out, but this is my take.” Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation into the 2018 scandal despite the fresh allegations. Wasim’s intervention, however, has added further weight to a debate that continues to divide opinion over what players knew during one of the most damaging episodes in Australian cricket. More than eight years after the Newlands incident, the renewed controversy has once again put the Australian team’s conduct and the credibility of its account of events under scrutiny.

items.title: Tunisie | L’Upmi appelle à réduire la taxe sur la consommation
items.description: Les membres de l’Union des petites et moyennes industries ( Upm i) appelle le ministère des Finances à réduire la taxe sur la consommation dans le cadre du projet de budget de l’État pour 2027. Cette taxe les contraint à augmenter les prix de leurs produits, ce qui entraîne une baisse des ventes et, par conséquent, une diminution des recettes de l’État provenant de ce tissu économique essentiel, a déclaré Wissem Ben Amor, son président, sur les ondes de Mosaïque , le vendredi 13 novembre 2026. Une réduction de cette charge fiscale permettrait aux dirigeants des PME de réaliser des bénéfices sur leurs ventes en baissant les prix de leurs produits, générant ainsi des recettes fiscales pour l’État. À l’inverse, une hausse des prix pousserait les consommateurs à se tourner vers le marché parallèle, dont les opérateurs ne payent pas d’impôt ; une situation qui a déjà entraîné la perte de centaines de PME, l’éviction des produits tunisiens et un manque à gagner pour l’État en termes de recettes fiscales légales, le tout dans un contexte d’évasion fiscale sévère et croissante de la part des acteurs du secteur informel, a-t-il expliqué. M. Ben Amor a estimé, dans la même déclaration, que le projet de budget de l’État pour 2027 omet plusieurs mesures susceptibles de sauver des PME en difficulté et d’améliorer leur situation. Il a notamment souligné l’absence de mise à jour de la loi relative à la restructuration des entreprises en difficulté financière — dont la validité expire en décembre 2026 — précisant que les chefs d’entreprise attendent une révision et une prolongation de ce dispositif pour une durée supplémentaire de deux à cinq ans. Cette loi, qui expire en décembre 2026, ne concerne que les entreprises endettées envers des institutions financières, a rappelé le président de l’Upmi. Et bien que le projet de budget de l'État pour 2027 prévoie des avantages en faveur des nouveaux entrepreneurs, il ne propose aucune mesure nouvelle pour les entreprises établies de longue date qui traversent des difficultés, croulent sous des dettes fiscales et font face à une crise financière. Et ce, malgré trois années d’amnistie fiscale, une mesure d’une ampleur inédite dans l’histoire de la Tunisie. De nombreuses petites entreprises continuent de faire face à une situation difficile, a rappelé M. Ben Amor. La loi relative à la restructuration ne concerne que les sociétés endettées envers des institutions financières ; or, certaines entreprises éprouvent des difficultés financières sans pour autant avoir de dettes bancaires. Elles sont, en réalité, entravées par un manque de liquidités nécessaires pour régler leurs arriérés fiscaux et leurs cotisations sociales, ce qui affecte également le paiement des créances que ces entreprises détiennent sur l’État. Il a par ailleurs relevé un problème majeur auquel sont confrontées les PME : le décalage entre les textes législatifs et leur application concrète. Cette situation ne fait qu’aggraver les difficultés, tant pour les entreprises établies de longue date que pour celles créées plus récemment. Les textes législatifs, leur philosophie sous-jacente et leur mise en œuvre semblent évoluer dans des directions totalement divergentes, constatent les chefs d'entreprise membres de l’Upmi, ajoutant que même les entreprises bénéficiant d’un soutien à la restructuration, d’un montant de 300 000 dinars, se retrouvent à consacrer la totalité de cette somme au remboursement de dettes bancaires. Elles ne disposent ainsi d’aucune marge de manœuvre financière leur permettant de relancer leurs activités économiques, de production et de commercialisation ; elles se heurtent, par conséquent, de nouveau aux institutions financières, qui se montrent réticentes à leur accorder des crédits. I. B. L’article Tunisie | L’Upmi appelle à réduire la taxe sur la consommation est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Le Crédit populaire d’Algérie lance le paiement en ligne depuis l’étranger : mode d’emploi
items.description: Le Crédit Populaire d'Algérie (CPA) a annoncé jeudi 12 novembre le lancement d'un service de paiement en ligne depuis l’étranger via les Visa et Mastercard. Baptisée CPAzonepay, cette solution entre dans le cadre des efforts de la banque « en faveur de la transformation digitale et l'accompagnement de sa clientèle professionnelle ». La banque publique explique que cette solution de paiement en ligne est « destinée aux commerçants algériens souhaitant faciliter les transactions de leurs clients à l’international et développer leurs opportunités commerciales. » Paiement en ligne depuis l’étranger : le CPA lance sa solution À travers CPAzonepay , le CPA veut accompagner les commerçants dans la digitalisation de leur service de paiement et le développement de leur activité commerciale, en leur offrant la possibilité de commercialiser leurs produits et services en faveur d'une clientèle internationale, a-t-on ajouté. Elle permet aux clients des commerçants algériens de « régler leurs achats en ligne par carte Visa ou Mastercard, à tout moment », simplifie le « traitement des paiements » et offre aux clients un « parcours d’achat fluide ». CPAzonepay permet aussi « une ouverture à l'international par l'acceptation des paiements effectués depuis l'étranger, l'élargissement de la base clients en accédant à une clientèle internationale en plus de la locale, la gestion simplifiée des paiements et la fiabilité et la sécurité des transactions », souligne la même source. Mode d’emploi et conditions « Avec le lancement de CPAzonepay, le CPA réaffirme son engagement à mener à bien la stratégie de transformation digitale déjà amorcée. En proposant cette solution innovante, le CPA contribue efficacement à l'expansion des prestations et produits nationaux sur les marchés internationaux », ajoute le communiqué. Pour bénéficier du CPAzonepay, la banque a fixé trois conditions : · Disposer d’un site Web ou d'une application sécurisé avec panier d’achat et conditions générales de vente. · Avoir un registre de commerce ou une carte d’entrepreneur pour le commerce électronique. · Disposer de comptes en dinar et devise (USD) domiciliés au CPA. Ensuite, il faut remplir le « formulaire émis par votre agence CPA, intégrez CPAzonepay sur votre site, et commencez à recevoir des paiements internationaux ! » L’article Le Crédit populaire d’Algérie lance le paiement en ligne depuis l’étranger : mode d’emploi est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The accidental rebel – Loyalty, exile, and hidden burden of the stepchild, by Stephanie Shaakaa
items.description: In previous essays, I examined the emotional paradoxes of stepparenthood.The stepmother expected to provide sacrificial warmth without maternal equity, and the stepfather tasked with silent financial provision without moral authority. But there is another person in this arrangement whose experience deserves equal attention, perhaps even greater consideration. The child. In a family structure created by adults, the child is often the person with the least control over the arrangement, yet carries some of its heaviest emotional consequences. Adults choose each other, negotiate their relationships and decide how their lives will be reorganised. The child, however, is expected to adjust to decisions already made. What happens to the child who never chose the arrangement or have no vote in it, yet must live inside its consequences every day? The shift rarely announces itself through a dramatic confrontation. It happens quietly in the back seat of a car or before a hallway mirror, as a child, bag in hand, moves between two entirely different worlds. They step out of one parent’s home, where familiar rhythms, recognisable voices and unwritten rules define their existence. Twenty minutes later, they walk through another front door. There is a couch that smells different, an adult offering an overly deliberate greeting, and an unspoken expectation that they should instantly adjust their mood, unpack their life and feel at home. To the adults who have engineered this new chapter, that arrival represents hope and a second chance. But to the child holding the bag, it feels like an unchosen relocation. Society has a ready-made script for how children process this transition: the difficult stepchild. The label attaches itself the moment a child crosses their arms, offers a monosyllabic reply or retreats behind a closed bedroom door. They are quickly branded stubborn, ungrateful or defiant, a child apparently intent on sabotaging a happy home. Yet labelling a child’s distance as defiance fundamentally misinterprets what may be happening beneath the surface. That closed door is not necessarily an act of malice; it may be an act of emotional self-preservation. The child is not trying to tear down a marriage. They are trying to survive a profound disruption to their world, one in which they had no say. Adults choose each other; children are simply moved. Overnight, their personal geography is rewritten. New household rules take root, unfamiliar routines are enforced, and another adult occupies permanent space in their daily lives. Even when a stepparent is patient, kind and eager to connect, their presence changes the household. A space that once belonged entirely to the child’s original family story must now accommodate another person’s habits, expectations and authority. The result is a quiet, ongoing exile. The child becomes an occupant in a home that feels foreign, cared for and provided for, yet quietly displaced. The hardest part for a child isn’t sharing a bathroom or adapting to a new schedule. It is the quiet panic of feeling that being kind to a stepparent means turning their back on their own mother or father. When a stepparent reaches out with genuine warmth, perhaps through thoughtful advice, a gift or an attempt to bridge the divide, the child may pull back. To the adult, this withdrawal feels baffling and ungenerous. But to the child, accepting that warmth can trigger an emotional conflict they may struggle to understand, let alone explain In a child’s internal math, liking a stepmother can feel like a direct betrayal of the biological mother across town. Respecting a stepfather’s authority can feel like erasing the flawed or absent father they are still desperately holding on to. Every small step towards a stepparent feels dangerously close to treason against their origin. When a child grows distant, sharp or defensive, they may be guarding their past. They are defending their origin story against what feels like emotional erasure. A child who senses that fitting into a new house requires denying where they came from may resist that arrangement with everything they have. The resistance is not necessarily born of hatred. It may be the only way they know to preserve a sense of themselves. Faced with this internal pressure, children also learn to navigate the fault lines between households. Adults often complain that stepchildren are manipulative, that they play biological parents against stepparents, exploit disagreements between households or take advantage of inconsistencies in domestic rules. Yet what adults view as manipulation may sometimes be a child navigating the cracks of an unstable arrangement. When adults fail to establish clear boundaries and present a reasonably consistent approach to parenting, children naturally discover the gaps. In an environment where their position already feels uncertain, those gaps can become a means of retaining some control over their lives. This does not mean every act of manipulation should be excused, but understanding the insecurity beneath the behaviour is essential to addressing it. The fundamental mistake adults make is attempting to force an outcome. Stepparents sometimes try to buy affection or demand respect through their position in the household; biological parents may rush a happy-family narrative out of guilt over the past. Both approaches misunderstand the nature of belonging. Affection cannot be coerced, and belonging cannot be commanded into existence. The way forward requires adults to abandon the demand for instant intimacy and offer something far more durable: explicit emotional freedom. A child needs to know, through words and actions, that accepting a stepparent does not require abandoning a biological parent. They need permission to love both homes, dislike the friction between them or simply take their time without feeling that their loyalty is being examined at every turn. The biological parent must stop asking the child to pretend that nothing was lost. The stepparent, meanwhile, must resist the temptation to compete for a title and commit instead to being an unshakeable, non-competing mentor. A stepchild’s trust is never won by defeating their memories or replacing their past. It is earned through quiet consistency: an adult who sets clear boundaries without bitterness, offers kindness without expecting a reward, and respects the child’s history without feeling threatened by it. When adults stop treating a child’s distance as a personal insult and begin understanding it as a search for safety, the atmosphere in the home begins to change. The child no longer has to defend their past simply to make room for the present. A stepchild does not need to be conquered or converted. They simply need space to honour where they came from, while discovering that a new house can offer safety without requiring them to erase their past. Stephanie Shaakaa shaakaastephanie@yahoo.com 08078600871 The post The accidental rebel – Loyalty, exile, and hidden burden of the stepchild, by Stephanie Shaakaa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
items.description: AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety. The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon. Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP. Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models. Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue. But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP. Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous —AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector. ‘Human control’ “I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month. “China has no guardrails,” he said— except that “whatever President Xi says goes”. Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities. Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”. Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19. Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans. Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal. In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said. Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app. “Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time. “But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”. ‘Manipulation risks’ US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons. Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”. They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”. For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working. “The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs. For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China. It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said. “It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.” Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week. “Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP. More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

items.title: Tinubu’s aide dismisses claims of convoy stoning
items.description: O’tega Ogra, Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New Media, has disputed claims that the president’s convoy was attacked by youths following his attendance at Friday prayers at the Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Abuja. Tinubu had visited the mosque in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for the Juma’at prayer on Friday. However, Dino Melaye, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), later shared a video showing some youths throwing stones at a convoy believed to belong to the president. In the video, which has circulated widely on social media, some of the youths were heard chanting, “Ba ma yi, ba ma so”, a Hausa expression meaning “we don’t want you; we don’t support you”. Reacting to the development, Ogra shared a separate video showing Tinubu leaving the mosque after the prayers. “Contrary to the narrative being pushed by the opposition, with videos of their alleged paid thugs at the National Mosque today, here is footage of Mr President leaving the mosque after Friday prayers this afternoon,” Ogra wrote. The footage showed Tinubu, dressed in a white outfit and black cap, waving to youths who cheered him and took photographs with their mobile phones as he made his way into his official vehicle. Ogra’s response challenged the account circulating on social media. However, the footage he shared did not independently establish whether the incident captured in Melaye’s video occurred at another location along the president’s route. The development comes amid growing concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general election. In a statement he personally signed on Friday, Tinubu warned politicians and their supporters against resorting to violence, saying security agencies had been authorised to deal decisively with thuggery and other anti-democratic activities. He condemned reported incidents of violence at political events across the country and urged political actors to focus their campaigns on issues affecting the welfare of Nigerians and national development. The president reiterated that violence had no place in political campaigns. The post Tinubu’s aide dismisses claims of convoy stoning appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: What has changed for Asaba since Azinge became Asagba?
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi When HRM Prof. Epiphany Chigbogu Azinge, SAN, ascended the throne of the Asagba of Asaba two years ago, he inherited an institution steeped in history, tradition and expectations. Today, the palace is becoming something more. A smart school has been built by the community and handed to the Delta State Government. Ambulances respond to emergencies. A drug rehabilitation centre has emerged. Security intelligence flows into the palace within minutes. Public spaces are being upgraded, a 1000-capacity Event Centre hosted guests to Nna Agu’s second coronation anniversary. Women are gaining a stronger voice in traditional affairs. Even long-standing practices such as community burials are being reviewed. For Azinge, the change is deliberate. He declared, “I’ve long migrated from being a traditional ruler, and now into traditional governance. I’m not only trying to think about the customs and traditions of our people. “I’m also thinking about the welfare, healthcare, education, among so many other things, to make sure my people, Asaba people, collectively, are very happy going forward.” It is a philosophy beginning to redefine what many residents expect from their traditional institution, the people building for themselves Perhaps nowhere is the new relationship between palace and people more visible than at the Asaba Community Smart Nursery And Primary School recently commissioned and donated by Asaba to the Delta State Government. Asagba Azinge sees it more than a building. “Today, Asaba is breaking new grounds. We try to shatter ceilings, if and when the opportunity presents itself. “I believe in the history of Delta state, and I dare say of Nigeria, this is the first time a community will come together, not just to build a smart school, but also have it donated to government” The project, he said, demonstrates that the traditional institution can mobilise the community while government provides the broader public-service framework. “It underscores our willingness, readiness at all times to partner our state government, complement their efforts, and support them in the growth and development of our state and our community in particular.” But the partnership comes with expectations. Standing at the school, Azinge turned to the government with a simple request: “If Asaba can donate a school to you, please donate a road to us so we can achieve this. Donate a road so people can access this place easily and then be able to school here.” For Delta State Commissioner for Primary Education, Chief Mrs Rose Ezewu, the message was equally clear. “This occasion is significant not merely because we are unveiling a new school facility, but because we are witnessing the power of community vision, responsible leadership and purposeful partnership in advancing the cause of education. “Sustainable progress requires collaboration with communities, traditional institutions, parents and other stakeholders.” A Palace That Listens If the school represents physical development, security represents less visible change. When officers of the Defence Intelligence College, Abuja, visited Asaba, Azinge described an intelligence network that puts the palace at the centre of community security. “Nothing happens in this kingdom I don’t get to hear within five minutes. Good or bad, it filters into the palace, so I get to know. “It is my duty and responsibility, as the ruler of Asaba, to determine where to divert such information, depending on severity and the agency best suited to handle the issue at hand.” The system, he said, depends on trust, “We have cultivated confidence from those who provide such intelligence. We preserve their confidentiality and privacy, and they believe their identity will never be disclosed in a way that will jeopardize their lives.” A vigilante outfit works with the Police, DSS and other agencies, while security is reviewed every Tuesday. “We identify potential flashpoints, brainstorm and come up with ideas to mitigate threats before they escalate,” he said. It is traditional authority operating in a distinctly modern way: gathering information, coordinating institutions and attempting to prevent crises before they happen. From Ceremonies To Welfare At the second anniversary thanksgiving Mass at St. Patrick’s Catholic Church, Asaba, Rev. Fr. Peter Muobogwu offered another perspective. “We are thankful to God for the celebration of today because God has visited us and blessed us with a visionary Asagba. “It is not a fairy tale or folklore that among the humanitarian services of the Asagba of Asaba, there are functional ambulances. “Within this period, those who are in emergency health situations can put a call across and can be taken to the hospital.” A drug rehabilitation centre has also been established, expanding the palace’s intervention into an area traditionally left almost entirely to government and specialised institutions. With the people watching, the strongest measure of the new model may ultimately be how they perceive it. Chairman of the anniversary committee, Chief Amb. Charles Onianwa, said, “The people of Asaba felt it wise to honour the Asagba whose achievements over the past two years have been unmatched. “He has taken bold steps for the good of Asaba and its people. We are holding this celebration to express our gratitude and say, ‘Thank you, Nna Agu, for all you have done.’” Chief Victor Nwosa, Awulika Asaba, was more direct: “He has done so much for Asaba within this short period. So we are encouraging him to do more.” The list also includes the beautification of Ogbeke Square and upgrading of the Kainebisi Roundabout with Providus Bank’s support Ogbueshi Dr Jude Mgbeze, Asagba’s Private Secretary, underscored the new place for women within the traditional structure. He noted, “He has raised status of women in Asaba. First, he has made them proper chiefs on their own. Whether your husband is a chief or not, if you are good enough, he makes you a chief” REVIEWS Azinge’s approach has not meant abandoning tradition. Rather, he has shown willingness to bend convention when he considers it necessary. He had announced he would not confer chieftaincy titles until 2027. He made an exception for renowned environmentalist and businessman, Chief Newton Jibunoh, whom he decorated as ‘Odenigwe Ahaba’. “I ascended the throne 5 October 2024. And I made it very clear I would not confer any chieftaincy until 2027. But nothing is cast in stone. When it became absolutely necessary for me to shift ground, I had to because of Chief Newton Jibunoh.” Significantly, Jibunoh is not an Asaba indigene. “We don’t often confer titles on non-indigenes,” Azinge said, explaining that the required approval from Jibunoh’s home traditional ruler was obtained. The episode captured something fundamental about the monarch’s approach: tradition remains important, but it can be reviewed. A New Compact With Government For the Delta State Government, the emerging model presents both opportunity and responsibility. The smart school illustrates the arrangement: the community provides an asset; government assumes responsibility for integrating it into public education system. Azinge’s challenge for a road in return makes the relationship reciprocal. Yet the monarch insists the transformation cannot be credited to the palace alone. “Leadership without followership is as good as dead. I draw a lot of strength and inspiration from the teeming Asaba people who have graciously donated their time, talent, and treasure to whatever we have been doing.” Two years into his reign, perhaps that is the clearest change in Asaba: the palace is no longer being presented merely as a place where tradition is preserved, but increasingly as a place where community problems are identified, people mobilised and government challenged to respond. And Asagba Azinge believes much more is coming.n“This is just a tip of the iceberg,” he said. For a city watching its traditional institution evolve, the next two years may reveal whether Azinge’s experiment in “traditional governance” can turn the momentum of a remarkable beginning into a lasting model for Asaba. items.title: Why 16 Nigerians died transiting through Addis Ababa
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has advised Nigerians, particularly those with underlying health conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the death of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued the advisory on Friday, revealing that Nigeria’s diplomatic mission in Addis Ababa recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the Ethiopian capital. The deaths were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. According to the ministry, Addis Ababa is located about 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen levels. The ministry noted that while most healthy individuals can adapt to such conditions, travellers with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory illnesses may face increased health risks. “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitude,” the statement said. The government therefore urged Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high-altitude environments to seek medical advice before travelling through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are strongly advised to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys,” the ministry stated However, the Federal Government stressed that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. “Rather, it aims to ensure that persons who may be medically vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes are adequately informed and encouraged to take necessary precautions,” the statement added. The ministry reaffirmed the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians abroad through timely travel advisories and other consular support measures. items.title: Stench of ‘Sandpapergate’ set to linger as scandal reignites
items.description: Australian captain Pat Cummins wants to draw a line under “ Sandpapergate ” and move on, but the stench of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is set to linger after a week of sensational accusations and denials . Cummins held an intense 70-minute press conference on Friday and answered every question thrown at him after former teammate Usman Khawaja reopened old wounds with the release of his explosive autobiography. In the book, he claimed the whole team, including Cummins, knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa. Only David Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were held responsible by Cricket Australia for the incident that shattered the nation’s reputation, with all three sent home in disgrace and banned. Cummins repeated multiple times that he was not aware of the plan, insisting Khawaja’s version of events was “100 per cent wrong”. “I don’t want to talk about this again after today… because at some point we’ve got to move on,” he added. His plea drew support from Justin Langer, who took over as head coach when Darren Lehmann quit in the wake of the scandal. “Hopefully, that will put some sort of line in the sand because we have to move on,” Langer told SEN radio. “There are too many people being hurt in Australian cricket… and that includes the Australian public. “When I talk about Australian cricket, it’s about the public, it’s about the fans, it’s about the players, it’s about everyone who’s involved: the past players, the present players, future players. We have to draw a line in the sand somewhere.” Another former Test great, Greg Chappell, also urged an end to the in-fighting. “We don’t want to see Australian cricket eating itself and having a little spat within the family,” he told reporters. “Hopefully Pat’s put a bit of a line under it and we can start getting on with the summer of cricket.” While calls to put the issue to bed mount, it could blow up again with several key players yet to comment, notably Smith and Bancroft, while Khawaja has media commitments to sell his book. Warner has strongly backed close friend Khawaja’s new version of events, making clear he will not rest “until the truth is out there”. He ratcheted up the pressure on Saturday, claiming Cricket Australia’s investigation “stinks of a cover-up”. Pick your side “The biggest error of the Cummins Q and A was his belief that his appearance would allow everyone to draw a line under the affair and move on,” national broadcaster ABC said in an analysis. “That’s not happening. We’re dealing with hurt feelings here, fractured relationships and bruised egos and nebulous concepts of truth and justice. “You better pick your side, if you haven’t already, because this is never going away.” Whether what really happened is ever properly established remains to be seen, with Cricket Australia adamant it will not be reopening its investigation. But the bonds of a 15-year friendship between Cummins, Khawaja and Warner have splintered. Cummins accused Khawaja of being “flippant and casual” by dropping his bombshell claims eight years after the fact, suggesting some of them were “probably defamatory”. That prompted Warner to blast Cummins for throwing Khawaja “under the bus” and The Australian newspaper to declare that “a generation of Australian players is officially at war”. Cummins insists unity within the current Australian team, which includes Smith, remains strong despite the week’s firestorm as they prepare for a home Test series against New Zealand in December-January. He said he had spoken to Smith, who lost the captaincy and was banned for a year over “Sandpapergate”, and suggested the veteran batsman was keen not to regurgitate the past. “I have spoken to Smithy. Without breaking confidence, he is done with this; he wants to move on,” said Cummins. “This was very traumatic for him. If standing up today and answering all your questions helps everyone move on, then maybe it’s a good thing.”
